name: MonarchTableToolbar
title: TableToolbar
summary: The bar above a table or list: a search field, filters, the result count and the app's controls (view switcher, column menu, actions); while rows are selected the search and filters give way to the bulk selection bar.
whenToUse: Above a table, a data grid or a long list that people search, filter, switch between views or select from, such as a list of contacts or invoices.
whenNotToUse: For a screen-wide title and actions, use the top app bar. For actions on selected items without search or filters, use MonarchBulkActionBar on its own.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTableToolbar(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, resultCount: Int? = null, selectedCount: Int = 0, totalCount: Int? = null, bulkActions: List<MonarchBulkAction> = emptyList(), onClearSelection: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchTableToolbarLabels = MonarchTableToolbarLabels(), search: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, filters: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, controls: @Composable () -> Unit = {})
class MonarchTableToolbarLabels(toolbar: String? = null, results: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, bulkActionBar: MonarchBulkActionBarLabels = MonarchBulkActionBarLabels())

options.name: resultCount
options.description: Rows that match the search and filters, shown as "N results" in the locale's digits and announced when it changes. null hides the count.

options.name: selectedCount
options.description: Selected rows. While it is above 0 and onClearSelection is set, MonarchBulkActionBar replaces the search and the filters.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: Rows that could be selected, for "3 of 120 selected".

options.name: bulkActions
options.description: Actions on the selected rows, shown in the bulk selection bar.

options.name: onClearSelection
options.description: Empties the selection. Without it there is no bulk selection bar.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the TalkBack name of the toolbar, the result count text and the strings of the bulk bar.

options.name: search
options.description: A search field, such as MonarchSearchBar, first in the start part. Hidden while rows are selected.

options.name: filters
options.description: Filter controls, such as MonarchChips, in a row that scrolls sideways when it does not fit. Hidden while rows are selected.

options.name: controls
options.description: The trailing controls: a SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow as the view switcher, a Columns MonarchMenu and actions. They wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.

states.name: narrow
states.description: Below 640dp, or when the count and controls need more than half the width: the search and filters (or the bulk bar) take the first line and the count and controls the next, aligned to the end.

states.name: wide
states.description: From 640dp, when the count and the controls take at most half the width: the start part and the end part share one line, vertically centered.

states.name: selecting
states.description: With onClearSelection and a selection, MonarchBulkActionBar with the count, the bulk actions and Clear selection replaces the search and filters; the count and the controls stay.

states.name: no count
states.description: Without resultCount only the controls are in the end part.

appearance: No surface of its own: the controls sit on the screen's background. The result count is caption text in the muted text role; the bulk bar is MonarchBulkActionBar's raised surface. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web toolbar draws its own SearchInput, ViewSwitcher and ColumnMenu from props. On Android these are slots: the app passes MonarchSearchBar, a MonarchSegmentedControl and a Columns MonarchMenu (the view-switcher and column-menu recipes), so their state stays in the app. iOS has no search slot because search belongs to the navigation bar there (searchable); an Android screen has no such place, so search is a slot here. The web's sm and md sizes are not offered: the slotted controls keep their own sizes. The web's bulkChildren and returnFocusRef are not offered; focus after Clear selection follows TalkBack. The web keeps an uncontrolled search mounted while selecting; here search state is hoisted in the app, so the hidden field loses nothing. The layout decision (one line or two) is made from the measured width, not from the window size class, so the toolbar adapts inside panes.
accessibility: The toolbar is a traversal group named "Table controls", so TalkBack reads its controls together.
The result count is a polite live region: a new count is read without moving focus.
While rows are selected the bulk bar announces the count and "Selection cleared" when it empties, through MonarchBulkActionBar.
The controls wrap and the count text wraps at the largest font scale; nothing is cut.
The slotted Material 3 controls keep their own roles and 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A selectedCount above 0 without onClearSelection keeps the search and filters: there is no bulk bar to clear it.
Many filters scroll sideways in one line rather than pushing the controls down.
Inside a pane narrower than 640dp the toolbar uses two lines even on a large screen.
The count uses plurals in strings_tabletoolbar.xml with the number formatted for the locale; pass labels.results to write it differently.

parityExceptions.reason: The web label of this button joins its visible text and hidden text with no separator; on Android the button is named with a sentence for TalkBack and its visible text is shown as it is.
parityExceptions.convention: a control is named in a sentence, not by concatenated visible text (Material accessibility)
